title: A Route That Changes by Noon
transcript: A group of volunteers began mapping which sidewalks a wheelchair user could travel along near a public market. During their first outing, they marked curb ramps and measured narrow sections with a tape measure. A wheelchair user later joined the group and pointed out that a ramp can be wide enough yet still difficult to cross if the approach slopes sharply. The volunteers added a field for the slope and revisited several corners. They also discovered that delivery carts blocked a passage around lunchtime. The finished map included the time of each visit so readers could judge how well an observation might apply to their own trip.

questions.prompt: What did the wheelchair user help the volunteers realize?
options: The surface material mattered most on narrow sidewalks.
A ramp could be difficult to use even if it was wide enough.
Corners with the widest ramps usually had the least traffic.
Ramps near a market were more useful in the morning.
questions.answer: A ramp could be difficult to use even if it was wide enough.
questions.explanation: 轮椅使用者指出，即使坡道够宽，通往坡道的路面太陡也会使通行困难。

questions.prompt: Why did the map include the time of each visit?
options: To help readers judge whether conditions might be similar when they travel
To estimate how long each route would take to complete
To tell readers when the volunteers would next be available
To show which streets the volunteers had visited most often
questions.answer: To help readers judge whether conditions might be similar when they travel
questions.explanation: 记录观察时间能帮助读者判断，当时的通行情况是否也可能出现在自己出行的时段。
